rcrg-01-c1.quote: Anthropologists briskly adopted, but did not invent, the term 'cargo cult'.
rcrg-01-c1.claim: Anthropologists didn't coin the term, but within a few years some of them, including Lucy Mair and Ian Hogbin, had taken it up.

rcrg-06-c2.quote: Hong in January 1851 announced the establishment of a Christianity-based state called Taiping Tianguo (Heavenly Kingdom of Grand Peace)
rcrg-06-c2.claim: In January 1851, at Jintian, Hong proclaimed the Taiping Tianguo, the Heavenly Kingdom of Great Peace.

rcrg-04-c1.text: Ghost Dance. Encyclopedia of the Great Plains / Encyclopedia.com.
rcrg-04-c1.quote: His health was seriously affected by scarlet fever until he made a dramatic recovery on 1 January 1889, a day that coincided with a total eclipse.
rcrg-04-c1.claim: Wovoka said that during the solar eclipse of 1 January 1889, while gravely ill, he was taken to the other world

rcrg-04-c2.quote: Many Lakota also believed that the Ghost Dance would make them invincible against whites, providing them with magic talismans, such as “ghost shirts,” which would stop army bullets.
rcrg-04-c2.claim: Many believed the shirts had protective power, and some said they would stop bullets.

rcrg-04-c3.quote: The event, known as the Wounded Knee Massacre, was termed a 'battle' by the US government, and 20 of the soldiers who participated in it were given the Medal of Honor.
rcrg-04-c3.claim: About twenty soldiers later received the Medal of Honor.

rcrg-05-c3.quote: In his book The Dead Will Arise: Nongqawuse and the Great Xhosa Cattle-Killing Movement of 1856-7, historian JB Peires contends that by May 1857, 400,000 cattle had been slaughtered and 40,000 Xhosa had died of starvation.
rcrg-05-c3.claim: Peires estimates that about 400,000 cattle were killed and about 40,000 Xhosa died of starvation

rcrg-05-c2.quote: She saw the departed ancestors who told her that if people would but kill all their cattle, the dead would arise from the ashes and all the whites would be swept into the sea.
rcrg-05-c2.claim: In return the dead would rise, new and healthy cattle would fill the kraals, grain pits would overflow, and the settlers would be swept into the sea.

rcrg-03-c1.text: Remote tribes mourning the loss of their god-like figure, Prince Philip. CBS News.
rcrg-03-c1.quote: Some villagers have come to believe Prince Philip is the fulfillment of a prophecy of a tribesman who "left the island, in his original spiritual form, to find a powerful wife overseas,"
rcrg-03-c1.claim: Philip "left the island, in his original spiritual form, to find a powerful wife overseas."

rcrg-03-c2.text: Vanuatu tribe mourns the death of its fallen god, Prince Philip. Global News.
rcrg-03-c2.quote: Prince Philip had an off-camera meeting with five tribespeople in 2007, after a reality TV show arranged to fly them to the U.K. for the encounter.
rcrg-03-c2.claim: Their trip ended with a private, off-camera meeting with the Duke, at which they exchanged gifts and received a new photograph.

rcrg-02-c1.text: Jon Frum. The Concise Oxford Dictionary of World Religions.
rcrg-02-c1.quote: A mysterious figure, Jon Frum (variously understood as an ancestor, the local mountain god, Karaperamun, or the ‘King of America’, after contact with affluent American troops in Second World War )
rcrg-02-c1.claim: Many Tannese say instead that John Frum was a spirit, linked by some to Keraperamun, a god of Mount Tukosmera.

rcrg-02-c3.quote: Today, John Frum is both a religion and a political party with a member in Parliament.
rcrg-02-c3.claim: Since then the movement has fielded candidates in national elections, and in 1998 one won a seat in parliament.
